note: One strong reading per PPDT picture (D33), shown after the candidate's own attempt. Each has a hero near the candidate's age, a realistic problem, positive action and an outcome: past, present, future. Not the answer: one way among many.

samples.ppdt-01: Kunal, a 20-year-old engineering student, was waiting on platform 1 for the 12:50 train home. He saw a man on crutches making for the coach while an older woman, his mother, watched anxiously beside their bags. With two minutes left, Kunal asked a fellow traveller to keep an eye on the luggage, helped the man up the steps and lifted the bags in after him. On the journey he learnt the man had lost his leg in a flood rescue. Moved by the story, Kunal joined the NCC that term and later went on to train as a disaster-relief volunteer in his district.
samples.ppdt-02: Naik Dorje, 24, was leading a four-man patrol across a rock face to reach a stranded survey team before nightfall. A loose ledge had cut off the usual path, so he roped the team together and chose a longer line across firmer rock. When the last man slipped, Dorje anchored the rope and held him until the others pulled him up. They reached the surveyors by dusk, shared their rations and guided them down the next morning. The company commander later used Dorje's route to mark a safer track for every patrol that followed.
samples.ppdt-03: Ritu and her two classmates, Sameer and Aman, had a week to finish a project on rainwater harvesting for their college. They met on the lawn every evening, divided the reading and checked each other's sums on the laptop. When they found their storage figures did not add up, Ritu suggested visiting a nearby village that already harvested rain. The farmers there showed them a working system and its costs. The team rebuilt the model with real numbers, won the inter-college prize, and the principal decided to fund a tank for the hostel.
samples.ppdt-04: Rohan, a 23-year-old junior engineer, had found a calculation error in a bridge design due for approval that week. At the review he stood and pressed the point hard, while a senior colleague argued from his chair that the schedule could not slip. The project head smiled and asked Rohan to show his numbers. He walked them through the loads step by step until the error was plain to all. The design went back for a fortnight's rework, and the bridge later opened safely. Rohan was asked to check every design that came after.
samples.ppdt-05: In Sarangpur the well was the village's only water through the summer, and that year it was running low. Before dawn, Bhola, a 19-year-old farmer's son, gathered the young men and women who came to draw water and proposed they deepen the well and clean the channel that fed it. They worked in shifts every morning for a week, before the fields needed them. The panchayat lent ropes and a pump. By the next monsoon the well held water till April, and the neighbouring village asked the group to help them do the same.
samples.ppdt-06: Constable Ramesh was on an early patrol in the fog when he found an old man walking alone near the main road, confused and shivering. He sat him down, gave him his own shawl and gently asked his name and village. The man remembered only a temple near his home. Ramesh radioed the station, checked the missing-person reports and learnt a family nearby had been searching since midnight. He drove the old man home himself. His son thanked Ramesh, and the station later began a register of elderly residents so such searches could be quicker.
samples.ppdt-07: Neha, 22, had stayed up past midnight finishing a project report due at nine the next morning. Tired and stuck on the final section, she rested her head in her hand and felt like giving up. Then she remembered her mentor's advice to break a big task into small steps. She listed what remained, finished the charts first and wrote the conclusion in short points. By two she had a complete draft and slept for four hours. Her presentation the next day went well, and the company later offered her a place on the project team.
samples.ppdt-08: Kavita, a 26-year-old teacher, received a letter from home saying her father had fallen ill and the harvest was due in a week. Worried, she read it twice, then sat down to plan. She spoke to her headmistress, who arranged for a colleague to take her classes for ten days. She called her cousin, a nurse, to visit her father the same evening, and booked the morning bus. At home she organised the harvest with the neighbours' help while her father recovered. She returned to school on time, and later set up a phone tree for the village's elderly.
samples.ppdt-09: Two brothers, Mohan and Sukhdev, were digging a channel across their field at sunrise to bring water from the canal before the dry spell set in. The ground was hard, and their neighbours said it could not be done in time. They worked in turns each morning, raising their pickaxes high to break the crust, and asked the canal officer for permission to open a small gate. Within ten days the water reached their wheat. The crop was saved, and the next year three neighbouring farmers joined them to extend the channel.
samples.ppdt-10: At the river ghat one winter morning, an old woman slipped on the wet steps and could not stand. Vikas, a 21-year-old student who had come for a dip with his friends, saw her fall. He told his friends to hold her gently under the arms while a woman nearby supported her back, and together they lifted her out and sat her on a dry step. Vikas called her son and found an auto to take her to the clinic, where a sprained ankle was treated. Later he asked the ghat committee to fit a handrail, and it was put up within the month.
